mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real estate sales (HOUST) signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the periods with declining HOUST, or if the correlation between HOUST declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within the last month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which increases corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 in the last month, it indicates a tight labor market with strong job growth, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% in the last month, it signals an inflationary environment with tight monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% within the last month, coupled with an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2%, signals a weakening consumer demand and labor market, which reduces corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases > 1% and UNRATE increases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint effect of RSAFS and UNRATE on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% signals a strong economic expansion, which increases corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods with increasing GDPC1, or if the correlation between GDPC1 increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
